scope: HGTXR-SW metric/protocol bridge for submission target comparison

protocol_contract.submission_split_claim: Following EX-Gaze, the submission draft adopts a dataset split protocol.

bridge_guard.reason: Coordinate frame, split protocol, hybrid scheduler mode, and P1 metric coverage are not yet matched.

coordinate_sanity_evidence.conclusion: metric_*_center_px and P5/P10 are measured after ROI/sensor spatial transform, not in raw EV-Eye sensor pixels.

bridge_blockers: Current metric_track_center_px is not confirmed to use the same pixel frame as the paper's 0.1812 px claim.
Current P10/P5 thresholds are in transformed input coordinates; sensor-space equivalence is anisotropic under the observed ROI transform.
Current active software queue is track/evaluator-focused and does not yet prove the full hybrid scheduler policy used by the submission table.
Submission P1 now has an evaluator metric key, but paper-frame full-test P1 evidence is not yet available.
Latency/hardware claims must remain separate from software accuracy promotion until a stronger full-width teacher exists.
required_evidence_to_unblock: Prediction rows with raw sensor-space center and transformed center for the same samples.
Evaluator path that either inverse-transforms track predictions to sensor pixels or replays the submission evaluator in the same coordinate frame.
EV-Eye split manifest counts and provenance matched to the EX-Gaze-following split claim.
Hybrid scheduler evaluation rows containing search/track mode, chosen state, P10/P5/P1, and center error for the same target definition.
A documented rule for whether software promotion uses transformed-input gates or paper-frame sensor-pixel gates.
experiment_implications: Use current center/P10/P5 gates for software promotion until the bridge is unblocked.
Keep XR-64-prep/XR-64A/XR-64B as P0 because they can improve trainable supervision without changing metric frame.
Do not claim progress toward 0.1812 px from current metric_track_center_px alone.
Add bridge verification before any final accuracy-closure claim.
